title: Empowered Committee Reviews Proposals to Accelerate Growth of Women-led Rural Enterprises
body_text:
The Empowered Committee of the Ministry of Rural Development, chaired by the Secretary (Rural Development), Shri Rohit Kansal, today considered proposals under the Non-Farm Livelihoods (NFL) component of DAY-NRLM to strengthen and scale up women-led rural enterprises and create a pathway for small-scale SHG enterprises to graduate into higher-order, growth-oriented businesses .
Shri Amit Shukla, Joint Secretary (Rural Livelihoods), and Ms. Swati Sharma, Joint Secretary (Rural Livelihoods), were also present at the meeting. The discussions focused on accelerating entrepreneurship-led livelihood opportunities for rural women and contributing to the national goal of making 6 crore Lakhpati Didis .
The Committee considered four new Incubator proposals from Bihar, Jammu & Kashmir, Uttar Pradesh and Gujarat , with IIT Patna, IIM Jammu, IIM Lucknow and IIT Gandhinagar , respectively, as the proposed incubator partners. The proposals were presented by the Principal Secretaries/Secretaries of the respective States, along with the State Mission Directors/CEOs of the SRLMs and representatives of the proposed incubator institutions. Together, the four programmes are proposed to support 600+ high-potential rural enterprises through structured interventions in business strategy, mentoring, financial planning, formalisation, technology adoption, market access and access to finance.
The Incubator Sub-Scheme builds on the experience of four completed incubator programmes in Assam, Bihar, West Bengal and Karnataka , which supported over 600 SHG enterprises . The programme has since expanded significantly, with 14 incubator programmes currently operational across 13 States, supporting around 2,100 rural SHG enterprises through partnerships with premier business and academic institutions including IIMs, IITs and leading incubation institutions. The earlier programmes demonstrated tangible outcomes, including revenue growth, improved business formalisation and additional employment generation.
The new incubators will focus on sectors such as food and agri-processing, textiles and handicrafts, manufacturing, retail and services, tourism-linked activities, digital enterprises and other locally relevant growth sectors . A key feature is a transparent, merit-based Challenge Fund for selection of enterprises with strong growth potential, along with dedicated State Incubation Cells to institutionalise enterprise support within the State Rural Livelihoods Missions.
The Committee also considered proposals for expansion of the Start-up Village Entrepreneurship Programme (SVEP) in West Bengal and Goa , aimed at further strengthening the rural non-farm entrepreneurship ecosystem and enabling more SHG members to establish and grow sustainable enterprises.
These initiatives reinforce the Government’s commitment to women-led economic development and the Lakhpati Didi initiative , by enabling rural women entrepreneurs to progress from subsistence-level businesses to enterprises with higher turnover, stronger market linkages, improved access to finance and greater employment potential.
The Empowered Committee emphasised innovation, institutional partnerships, convergence, digital adoption, market access and outcome-based monitoring , with the objective of creating a robust national ecosystem for incubation and sustained growth of women-led rural enterprises under DAY-NRLM.

enrichment.summary: The Empowered Committee of the Ministry of Rural Development, chaired by Secretary Rohit Kansal, reviewed proposals under DAY-NRLM's Non-Farm Livelihoods component to scale up women-led rural enterprises. It approved four new Incubator Sub-Scheme proposals for Bihar, Jammu & Kashmir, Uttar Pradesh and Gujarat, partnering with IIT Patna, IIM Jammu, IIM Lucknow and IIT Gandhinagar respectively, to support over 600 high-potential SHG enterprises. The Committee also considered expansion of the Start-up Village Entrepreneurship Programme (SVEP) in West Bengal and Goa.
enrichment.context:
DAY-NRLM (Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission) is India's flagship rural poverty-alleviation programme built around Self-Help Groups (SHGs) of rural women. Its Non-Farm Livelihoods vertical seeks to move SHG members beyond subsistence activities into higher-value enterprises, supporting the government's 'Lakhpati Didi' goal of enabling 6 crore rural women to earn sustainable annual household incomes above Rs 1 lakh. The Incubator Sub-Scheme, launched after pilot programmes in Assam, Bihar, West Bengal and Karnataka, partners with premier academic and business institutions (IIMs, IITs) to provide structured mentoring, financial planning, technology adoption and market linkages to SHG enterprises, aiming to institutionalise business incubation support within State Rural Livelihoods Missions (SRLMs).

This release reflects a scaling-up phase of an existing scheme rather than a new policy announcement — the incubator programme already operates in 14 locations across 13 states supporting around 2,100 enterprises, and this adds four more states. It is useful as an example of convergence between rural livelihoods missions and premier technical/management institutions, and illustrates the government's broader push on entrepreneurship-led rural transformation and financial inclusion of women, complementing other schemes like SVEP that support first-generation rural entrepreneurs.

prelims_questions.question: The 'Lakhpati Didi' initiative, aimed at enabling rural women to earn sustainable annual incomes above a threshold, is implemented under which scheme?
prelims_questions.explanation: The release states that the Non-Farm Livelihoods component under DAY-NRLM supports the national goal of creating 6 crore Lakhpati Didis, linking the initiative directly to NRLM.

prelims_questions.question: The Start-up Village Entrepreneurship Programme (SVEP), mentioned in context of rural enterprise expansion, primarily targets which group?
options: Urban unemployed youth under Skill India
Self-Help Group members in rural areas
prelims_questions.explanation: SVEP is a sub-scheme of DAY-NRLM designed to help SHG members establish and grow rural non-farm enterprises, as referenced in the release regarding its expansion in West Bengal and Goa.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the role of Self-Help Group (SHG)-based enterprise incubation models, such as those under DAY-NRLM, in fostering women-led rural entrepreneurship. What challenges must be addressed to help such enterprises graduate from subsistence to growth-oriented businesses?
Examine how convergence between rural livelihood missions and premier academic institutions (IITs/IIMs) can strengthen the ecosystem for rural entrepreneurship under schemes like DAY-NRLM.

study_notes.reason: The release carries testable factual core (DAY-NRLM, NFL vertical, Lakhpati Didi target, Incubator Sub-Scheme, SVEP) alongside genuine analytical material on convergence-based rural entrepreneurship models, so both study angles are legitimately present, though the release itself is a routine scaling update rather than a major policy shift.

prelims.point: DAY-NRLM (Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission) is built around women's Self-Help Groups (SHGs) and falls under the Ministry of Rural Development
prelims.why_important: DAY-NRLM is a flagship scheme frequently tested on objectives, ministry, and target group.

prelims.point: 'Lakhpati Didi' initiative aims to enable 6 crore rural women to earn sustainable annual household incomes above Rs 1 lakh
prelims.why_important: A specific numeric target under a named initiative is classic UPSC statement-matching material.

prelims.point: Start-up Village Entrepreneurship Programme (SVEP) supports first-generation rural entrepreneurs, distinct from the Incubator Sub-Scheme which targets high-potential SHG enterprises for scaling
prelims.why_important: UPSC often tests distinctions between similarly-purposed sub-schemes under the same mission.

prelims.point: Incubator Sub-Scheme under DAY-NRLM partners with premier academic/business institutions (IITs, IIMs) for mentoring, financial planning and market linkages of SHG enterprises
prelims.why_important: Tests knowledge of specific scheme mechanisms and institutional partnership models within rural livelihood missions.

mains.point: Convergence between rural livelihoods missions and premier technical/management institutions (IITs/IIMs) as a model for institutionalising business incubation support
mains.analytical_use: Useful for answers on innovative institutional mechanisms for scheme delivery or convergence-based governance models in welfare schemes.

mains.point: Enterprise graduation pathway — moving SHG members from subsistence-level activities to higher-order, growth-oriented businesses — reflects a shift in rural livelihoods policy from mere income support to entrepreneurship-led transformation
mains.analytical_use: Can be used in questions on strategies for rural non-farm employment generation or women's economic empowerment beyond microfinance.

mains.point: Use of a merit-based Challenge Fund and dedicated State Incubation Cells signals attempts to institutionalise outcome-based, competitive selection mechanisms within state rural livelihood missions
mains.analytical_use: Relevant for discussing innovative implementation/monitoring mechanisms in centrally sponsored schemes.

mains.point: Scaling of women-led rural enterprises contributes to financial inclusion and gender-responsive economic development, complementing broader goals of women's participation in the non-farm economy
mains.analytical_use: Supports answers on gender and inclusive growth, or the role of SHGs in rural economic diversification.

low_priority.reason: Administrative detail with no analytical or factual testability.
